summary: FFLA lists a standing tower at Martin NWR (Kedges Straits), Somerset County, Maryland. No build or fire history found; the refuge is closed to the public.

facts.status_note: Listed as standing by FFLA only; no other source found that describes the structure.
facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service manages the refuge; ownership of the tower is not stated

access.note: USFWS says the refuge is closed to the public to protect wetland habitats; much of it can be seen by boat.

evidence.supports: listed as a standing tower, Somerset County, coordinates
evidence.quote: Martin NWR – Kedges Straits Somerset 38.01444 -76.01778 Tower Standing

evidence.supports: refuge covers northern half of Smith Island in the Chesapeake Bay
evidence.quote: covering the northern half of Smith Island in the Chesapeake Bay

evidence.supports: refuge first established in 1954 through a 2,569 acre donation
evidence.quote: First established in 1954 through a 2,569 acre donation by the late Glenn L. Martin
Martin National Wildlife Refuge is closed to the public to protect wetland habitats.

evidence.supports: Wikipedia mentions a peregrine nesting tower installed in 1984
evidence.quote: Peregrine falcons have been nesting on the refuge every year since the first peregrine nesting tower was installed in 1984.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the FFLA entry is the only source naming a tower here. Two searches found no fire-lookout history for the Kedges Straits site. The Wikipedia article mentions a 1984 peregrine nesting tower on the refuge; it is not a fire lookout and is not treated as the FFLA structure. The FFLA coordinates are close to the refuge's Wikipedia coordinates but not identical. Access is set to closed from the USFWS page; the brief's 'unknown' is replaced. Wikipedia is used only as a lead for the refuge; the peregrine tower line is its own claim. Recommend confirming with FFLA or refuge staff what the entry refers to.
